la:verb:perbibo.html:
per-bĭbo, bĭbi, 3, v. a. (to drink much; hence), *
To drink or suck up: at ego perii, cui medullam lassitudo perbibit,.—
To drink in (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit., : lana quosdam (colores) non perbibit,: lacrimas,: medicamina,.—
Trop., to imbibe, receive: haec cum persuasi mihi et perbibi,: liberalia studia,: nequitiam, id. Ira, 1, 16, 2: mentes eorum penitus sucum stultitiae perbiberunt,: rabiem,: Latinum sermonem, Spald. N. cr.

la:adj:perbrevis.html:
per-brĕvis, e, adj.,
very short, very brief or concise: orator perornatus et perbrevis,: perbrevi tempore,.—Separate: altera pars per mihi brevis videtur,.—In abl.: perbrevi, adverbially,in a very short time,.—Adv.: perbrĕ-vĭter, very briefly, very concisely: quid sentiam, perbreviter exponam,

la:adv:perbene.html:
per-bĕnĕ, adv.,
very well: prandi perbene, Potavi,: pol ego

haud a pecuniā perbene, : loqui Latine,: Fortunam fecisse, quando, etc.,.

la:adv:perbreviter.gloss: very briefly, concisely, with very few words
senses: very briefly, concisely, with very few words

la:adj:perbonus.html:
per-bŏnus, a, um, adj.,
very good: prandium,: eam sei curabeis, perbona'st,: ager,: toreumata,: perbono loco res erat,.
